summary: Winding Stair Mountain lookout in Le Flore County, Oklahoma: 1934 and 1936 newspaper reports of a steel tower to replace a wooden one; now listed as removed.

facts.design: Steel fire tower, 33 ft, announced in 1936 to replace a 28-ft wood tower
facts.status_note: Listed as removed; the sources give no removal date.

events.note: June 22, 1934 (The Paris News, Texas): planned fire tower on Winding Stair Mountain, to be erected that autumn; completion not confirmed in the source
October 4, 1936 (Daily Oklahoman): 33-foot steel tower to replace the 28-foot wood tower in use; completion not confirmed in the source
October 4, 1936 (Daily Oklahoman): two tower guards named as stationed at the tower

sources.title: Sycamore (Forest Lookouts; transcribed clippings from The Paris News, 1934, and The Daily Oklahoman, 1936)

notes_for_editor: Dated evidence is two newspaper clippings, transcribed on the Central US Lookouts page; the originals were not checked. The 1934 clipping reports a plan, and the 1936 clipping describes a 28-foot wood tower already in use and a 33-foot steel tower to replace it. The record height (10.1 m) is the 33-foot figure, which is the planned steel tower; the wood tower's height is 28 ft. Elevation: the 1936 clipping gives 2,428 ft for the triangulation station, while the Winding Stair Mountains article gives 2,400 ft for the highest point; both are cited as given and not reconciled. Unread leads from search snippets only: a 2019 trip report with a 'Sycamore Lookout' photo caption mentioning towers and stone foundations near the high point; a 2012 Forest Service decision for a 20-year lease on an existing communications tower at a Sycamore site about seven miles east of Talihina (not confirmed as the lookout). No removal date or reason was found.
